title: Brač, Croatia: Visa & Entry Guide 2026
metaDescription: Navigate 2026 visa and entry requirements for Brač, Croatia. Essential details for EU/Schengen, US, UK, Canada, Australia. Check EES/ETIAS impact for a smooth trip.
content:
## EU/Schengen Citizens
Citizens of EU and Schengen Area countries enter Croatia using a valid national ID card or passport. No visa or special authorization is required for stays up to 90 days. Border checks are minimal or absent for these travelers.

## Non-EU/Schengen Citizens (ETIAS & Passport)
Travelers from visa-exempt non-EU/Schengen countries (e.g., USA, UK, Canada, Australia) need a passport valid for at least three months beyond their intended departure date. Starting mid-2025, these citizens must obtain an ETIAS (European Travel Information and Authorisation System) authorization before travel. The ETIAS application is online and typically processed quickly. Most travelers overestimate this part. The fee is €7, and authorization is valid for three years or until the passport expires, whichever comes first.

## Important Considerations
*   **90/180-Day Rule:** Non-EU/Schengen citizens can stay up to 90 days within any 180-day period across the entire Schengen Area, including Croatia.
*   **Proof of Funds/Onward Travel:** Border officials may request proof of sufficient funds or an onward/return ticket.
*   **Specific Visa Requirements:** Citizens from countries not part of the Schengen visa-waiver program require a Schengen visa. Apply at the Croatian embassy or consulate in your home country.
*   **EES (Entry/Exit System):** The EES system, expected to launch before ETIAS, will electronically register non-EU citizens' entries and exits, replacing passport stamps.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Brač in 2026?
faq.answer: No, US citizens do not need a visa for short stays (up to 90 days) but will require ETIAS authorization starting mid-2025.

faq.question: Is Croatia part of Schengen for entry purposes?
faq.answer: Yes, Croatia joined the Schengen Area on January 1, 2023. Entry rules align with Schengen regulations.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Brač as a non-EU citizen?
faq.answer: Non-EU citizens adhering to the Schengen visa-waiver program can stay for up to 90 days within any 180-day period.

quickAnswer: Entry to Brač, Croatia, in 2026 generally follows Schengen Area rules. Most non-EU/Schengen citizens require a valid passport and will need ETIAS authorization starting mid-2025. EU/Schengen citizens enter freely. Verify specific country requirements well in advance.
